set: B: one sheet of each acting state the page uses, confident, nervous, plain, scared, angry, shocked and exhausted, with no time and no word on it

issues.where: Below the lever throughout the spin, especially the last two frames
issues.what: The reels stop on a result without a readable reaction. The arrow keeps nearly the same default-pointer silhouette for most of the sheet.
issues.fix: Lean it toward the moving reels, tighten into a compressed waiting pose before the stop, then snap to a distinct held response on the result.

issues.where: First row at the crank and final two rows at the meter
issues.what: Only the first pose connects the arrow to the handle, so the crank appears to turn by itself. A held sideways pose shows attention to the meter, but the arrow barely changes as the bars light.
issues.fix: Keep its tip planted on the handle through a visible part of the turn, then give the meter a tense lean and one readable perk or recoil on a light change.

issues.where: Second-row launch and third-row stop between the dropdowns
issues.what: The directional stretch sells speed, but the arrow jumps out of a long neutral pose without winding up and returns to pointer shape with little compression or overshoot.
issues.fix: Add a low counterlean before departure and a short squash and rebound when it stops, then hold the settled pose.

issues.where: First-row ignition and the blurred upright poses in rows two and three
issues.what: The orange and smoke explain the heat immediately, but the body mostly rotates and blurs rather than producing a clear fright silhouette of its own.
issues.fix: Hold a clean kinked or pulled-back silhouette at ignition before the jitter, then stretch decisively in the escape direction.

issues.where: After the top-row wilt, through the final drop
issues.what: The wilt reads, but the crumpled shape loses much of the arrow's defining point and notch and then moves down almost unchanged. There is no distinct settling pose.
issues.fix: Keep a bent but recognizable point and notch in the melted shape, and add a small buckle or squash at the end of the drop.

issues.what: did not read: confident reads as tentatively curious: a pause, a dart, a steadying. Upright with a slight bounce and a strut is not in the read.
issues.fix: The strut of Confident: upright, a bounce in each step, held over a walk long enough to be seen.

issues.what: did not read: angry reads as alarmed and agitated: the glowing tip and the smoke are seen, and are taken for something happening to the arrow, not for its anger.
issues.fix: Anger as a pose before the heat: the arrow squared up to the thing it is angry at, held, and then the red tip and the steam.

issues.what: did not read: shocked reads as intent, then watchful and impatient. The double take, the stretch tall and the snap back are not in the read.
issues.fix: The double take of Shocked: the stretch tall, then the snap back to upright, held.

reads.read: Tentatively curious; the arrow comes into view beside two dropdowns, pauses, then darts right between them and steadies itself.
Alert, then briefly uneasy; the arrow perks up as the assessment text comes into view, bunches inward, then springs away toward the form fields.
Waiting, with no clear feeling beyond watchfulness; the birth-date reels spin and settle on 1991 while the arrow stays under the lever.
Startled, then dazed; coins burst from the slot, one appears to clip the arrow, and it recoils and slides away looking washed out.
Alarmed and agitated; the tip suddenly glows and starts smoking, and the arrow shakes and shoots upward to the strip that lights orange.
Intent, then watchful and impatient; the arrow starts beside the turning crank, races across the progress meter, and leans back toward it while more lights come on.
Spent and limp; the smoking arrow wilts into a crumpled shape as the crank stops, then sinks as the panel closes.
